integration_questions: Does the symmetric five-sensor sum stay above the 0.05 line-loss threshold on all development tracks?
Is the sensor spacing of 0.02 m fine enough to give a smooth signal, or does it saturate or jump at bend entries?
Does the 0.06 m forward offset help or hurt steering stability, judged against the signal lag it introduces?
Is the mass and yaw inertia at these values limiting turn response or causing wheel slip?

intent: Baseline geometry: a symmetric five-sensor forward array with graded overlap across the tape, moderate wheel track and radius, and low yaw inertia. It is meant to give the Integrator a stable, symmetric reading to tune against. The expected result is completion on the oval and s-bend with a small lateral error, and a slalom run that may show oscillation near the tighter bends.
learning: No prior evidence yet. Next iteration, use race telemetry (rms_error, max_error, steering_oscillation, line_loss_events) together with integration feedback to decide whether to widen or narrow the array, move the sensors forward or back, or change the wheel track, which sets turn authority.
rationale: This is the first iteration, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback yet. The design is a baseline built from the contract's limits. Five sensors at 0.012 m footprint, spaced 0.02 m apart and spanning ±0.04 m, cover about 80 mm across, which is more than three times the 25 mm tape width. That gives the controller a smooth, graded reading across the line and avoids the all-or-nothing loss of a narrow array. The sensors sit 0.06 m ahead of the axle, near the forward limit, so the robot reads the line before the wheels reach a bend. Wheel track is 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m, which are mid-range values that keep turn authority moderate. Mass is 0.7 kg and body length 0.14 m, which keeps yaw inertia low so the robot can turn quickly. Body width 0.12 m is enough: the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which evaluates to 0.06 m for any width up to about 0.19 m, so width has little effect on the limit. I expect a completable run on the development tracks, with the main uncertainty being whether the 0.06 m lookahead causes lag on tight slalom bends.
